[BERT4Rec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690) uses masked-item cross-entropy and trailing-mask inference; its paper also includes last-item-only masking during training. [Recency sampling research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.02643) motivates emphasizing recent interactions, but does not establish an optimal BERT4Rec endpoint distribution. Proposed implementation: sample a user uniformly, then endpoint t∈{2,…,n} from training history only; input the last L−1 items preceding t followed by the reserved MASK, target x_t, discard everything after t, and left-pad. Read the final MASK position, never nonpadding_count−1. Define p(t)∝exp[−β(n−t)/(n−2)] for n>2; β=0 gives uniform endpoints. Mix terminal-prefix examples with unchanged random Cloze examples using probability q; report q and β explicitly.

Retain full-catalog masked-item CE first: −s_positive+logsumexp(scores over real items), averaged over supervised positions; exclude padding/MASK classes. Compare against pairwise softplus on identical targets: L_pair=(1/K)Σ_j softplus(s_negative_j−s_positive). Specify K, sampling distribution, replacement policy, and exclusions using training interactions only. For hard negatives, sample M eligible candidates and select top H by detached current-model scores; define L=(1−α)mean_K(softplus_random)+α mean_H(softplus_hard), with explicit M,H,α. This keeps branch weights independent of negative counts. [Loss analysis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.07770) shows sampled CE and BPR coincide with one negative; multi-negative pairwise loss differs from joint sampled softmax.

Ablate Cloze/CE → uniform-terminal mixture/CE → recency-terminal mixture/CE, then cross endpoint policies with CE versus normalized pairwise loss; vary hard-negative weighting separately. Keep backbone, seeds, batches, epochs and evaluator fixed; report four-category macro validation HR@10 and GPU cost. Each experiment trains one model per category.
